title: Critical-path rotation and spotlight sprint lanes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and pilot a lightweight operating model that rotates the critical path across sprint lanes and reserves 'spotlight' lanes for high-urgency work. Goal: make mid-cycle decommits less disruptive, reduce single-team critical-path bottlenecks, and provide a predictable policy for scope cuts and emergency patches.
background: Over the last three cycles we've seen repeated all-or-nothing outcomes when a single initiative sits on the critical path. This concentrates risk, accelerates burnout for the owning squad, and forces blunt scope cuts late in the cycle. Several postmortems recommended experimenting with rotation and explicit 'spotlight' sprint lanes to spread risk and create a formal short-window handling process for urgent work.
proposal: Introduce two operational constructs: 1) Critical-path rotation: every two-week sprint, designate 1-2 initiatives as 'critical' and commit a time-boxed coordination cadence (wider stakeholders, daily unblock checks) while redistributing non-critical dependent tasks to adjacent sprints. 2) Spotlight sprint lanes: reserve 6-8 story points per squad per sprint for 48-72 hour high-urgency items; items run through a lightweight triage and pre-authorized guardrails to limit scope creep. Combine the constructs with a decision matrix for mid-cycle decommits and automatic reallocation of buffer capacity.
scope: Pilot with 3 initiatives across products: runtime, console UX, and dedicated capacity. Exclude security/legal-led work and regulatory releases. Pilot duration: two consecutive cycles (Cycle 2026-W12 and 2026-W13). Deliverables: decision matrix doc, triage checklist, sprint-board lanes template, and retrospective report with metrics.

acceptance_criteria: Decision matrix published and ratified by Eng leads and PM leads
Pilot runs for two cycles with at least 3 participating initiatives
Mid-cycle decommits are processed through the triage checklist and tracked
Post-pilot retrospective includes quantitative metrics and at least three documented lessons learned
Playbook entry and templates created and merged into internal repo
success_metrics: Mid-cycle decommit rate reduced by 30% for participating initiatives (vs. prior three-cycle baseline)
Cross-team blocker resolution time (median) reduced by 25% during critical rotation windows
Pulse survey: >=70% of participating engineers report clearer expectations on scope and handoffs
Number of out-of-band emergency context switches per squad reduced by 40%

dependencies: ENG-90123: telemetry event for decommit reason
PM-32455: cycle comms calendar slot for pilot kickoff
risks: Teams gaming spotlight lane by moving planned work into it — mitigated by triage checklist and guardrail enforcement
Measurement noise: baseline variability may obscure pilot impact — mitigated by using three-cycle baseline and descriptive comments
Operational overhead: extra cadence for rotating critical path could slow delivery if not time-boxed — mitigated by strict meeting templates and async updates
decisions: Adopt two-week rotation cadence aligned with sprint boundaries
Reserve up to 8 story points per squad per sprint as spotlight capacity
Exclude regulatory/security work from pilot to avoid confounding factors
